title: AstraScale Q3 Health + FinOps Alignment Workshop
summary: Quarterly health check focused on reducing per-token costs, improving 95th pct latency, and aligning on a phased pilot extension for private deployment. Customer raised data residency and KMS questions; Redwood proposed batching + prefix caching adjustments and a Dedicated capacity trial for peak hours.
action_items: Alex Chen - share updated pilot pricing spreadsheet by 2026-09-17
Priya Nair - run 2 workload-specific latency benchmarks and upload results by 2026-09-21
Sophie Kim (AstraScale) - confirm encryption-at-rest KMS vendor compatibility by 2026-09-20
next_steps: Send formal pilot amendment and pricing link
Schedule benchmarking session w/ AstraScale SREs (Priya + Marta + outsourced infra)
Share SOC2 + ISO docs and encrypted audit log example
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-13
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood), Priya Nair (Redwood), Marcus Holt (Redwood CSM), Elena Ortiz (Prod), Dana Lewis (AstraScale), Raj Patel (AstraScale), Sophie Kim (AstraScale Sec), Omar Ruiz (AstraScale FinOps), Marta Ivanova (AstraScale SRE)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time, um, quick roll call - i see dana, raj, sophie, omar, marta, and team from redwood. welcome. this is our Q3 health and finops alignment workshop. goal: get you to a pilot extension decision and actionables on cost/latency.
[00:18] Dana Lewis: thanks alex, appreciate it. we had a pretty busy quarter, traffic up ~3x on the ingestion side, and FinOps are seeing the invoice - little surprised.
[00:30] Omar Ruiz: yeah to be clear our biggest ask is: how do we cut token spend without making app latency worse? we rely on sub-300ms responses for widget flows.
[00:45] Priya Nair: totally — lifts and constraints matter. couple quick clarifiers — are the high-cost tokens mostly from long-context chat logs, or is it embed reruns?
[00:55] Dana Lewis: mix. chat for support assistant is long, and we also do nightly bulk embedding for similarity. the embedding job we can schedule differently, but the support path is what users notice.
[01:12] Raj Patel: and we have compliance: all support transcripts must be stored in eu-west-1 for residency and they need to be encrypted with our internal KMS (HashiCorp Vault currently).
[01:24] Sophie Kim: and on security, SOC2 is fine, but we need sample audit logs that show key rotation and who accessed KV caches — basically we need proof the platform supports our dedup and key access model.
[01:40] Marcus Holt: great callouts. we can provide audit-samples and the SOC2 pack. on KMS - Redwood supports customer-managed KMS providers; Priya can follow up on the Vault integration specifics.
[01:55] Priya Nair: yes, we have a Vault path baked in for Private deployments; for Hosted there are bring-your-key options too. small caveat: in hosted the key is wrapped by our HSM but can be customer-supplied, there was a doc we shared earlier — i'll re-share.
[02:10] Marta Ivanova: curious about Dedicated vs Hosted. we saw a couple latency spikes in August — 95th p exceeded 450ms a few times. can you explain root causes?
[02:23] Elena Ortiz: quick color — the spikes matched a model rollout where the new quantized variant had slightly different kernel selection, which temporarily affected warm-up and kv cache hit rates. our runtime team pushed a patch and the 95th dropped back.
[02:40] Dana Lewis: that's the kind of regression we want to avoid in prod — is there an automatic rollback?
[02:47] Priya Nair: yes, rollouts support canary + automatic fallback to previous model variant. you can tie policy to latency SLOs so that if 95th goes above threshold we revert.
[02:58] Omar Ruiz: ok but can you show cost math — e.g., if we move support assistant from Hosted to Dedicated reserved capacity for 100k monthly queries what happens?
[03:10] Alex Chen: fair — i'll summarize tabletop. rough numbers: Hosted at current usage and mix = $X per 1M tokens (we had detail in the deck), dedicated reserved with autoscale + prefix caching can reduce unit cost by around 28-45% depending on batching and off-peak utilization. will share updated sheet.
[03:30] Raj Patel: batch sizes worry us because some flows are latency-sensitive. what's the minimum latency impact if you enable micro-batching?
[03:42] Priya Nair: micro-batching (2-4 reqs) adds ~10-40ms median in our measures but reduces tokens/second cost materially. there's also intelligent workload-aware batching where public traffic gets batched and pinned low-latency routes bypass batching.
[04:00] Dana Lewis: so intelligent routing could solve tradeoff — route widget flows to low-latency pool, then batch background tasks.
[04:08] Priya Nair: exactly. we can map routes in the console and pin priority lanes.
[04:15] Sophie Kim: on audit and compliance - can you show an example log with the customer KMS thumbprint, rotated keys, and a sample of the admin actions? we need to send that to our audit team.
[04:28] Marcus Holt: we'll attach a redacted audit sample, and include key rotation metadata.
[04:35] Omar Ruiz: timeline — we need to decide whether we sign up for a dedicated reserve before next invoicing cycle (end of Oct). what is the pilot extension path and what decision gates do you recommend?
[04:48] Alex Chen: typical phased path: 1) small Dedicated trial for peak 4 hours/day (2 week burst test), 2) run benchmarks (latency + cost), 3) review and expand commit if ROI is there. decision gates: cost delta within 15-25% of forecast, no regression in 95th latency, and security check signed off.
[05:10] Marta Ivanova: ok can we do the benchmarks with our real traffic replay? we prefer real traffic so caches and sequence length distribution match.
[05:20] Priya Nair: yes, we can replay logs to a dedicated pool with prefix cache warm-up; we'll need a sanitized sample and a runbook for how to replay.
[05:30] Dana Lewis: note — embeddings run overnight; if we move that to non-peak dedicated windows we lower peak usage. also, consider quantizing the embedding model to 8-bit — what's the accuracy delta?
[05:44] Elena Ortiz: quantization recommendations vary by model; for many open quantized variants the embedding similarity delta is within noise for retrieval tasks, but we should validate on your prompts. that's part of the benchmark scope.
[05:58] Raj Patel: one more — network egress costs in eu-west-1 are non-trivial. do you have a pattern to lower egress (e.g., by colocating caches or using regional routing)?
[06:10] Priya Nair: yes route-by-region and edge prefix caching reduce cross-region egress. dedicated pools can be pinned to region to eliminate cross-region traffic.
[06:20] Omar Ruiz: finance will want to see a 6-month forecast with optimistic/pessimistic spend and break-even for reserved commit. can you supply that?
[06:30] Alex Chen: yes — action item for me to update the pilot pricing and a 6-month ramp forecast.
[06:38] [pause / cross talk while doc links are shared]
[06:55] Sophie Kim: i'm also asking about SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM provisioning and role-limited access to audit logs.
[07:05] Marcus Holt: we support SAML/SCIM and role-based access. you can limit 'view logs' to security roles. we'll include docs and a sample SCIM mapping.
[07:15] Dana Lewis: sounds good. maybe quick recap of the benchmark matrix so we can agree on what success means?
[07:22] Priya Nair: benchmark matrix: - latency: median & 95th on support flow; - quality: retrieval similarity and chat evals on 200 sample prompts; - cost: tokens per successful query & monthly cost projection; - stability: rollout canary pass/fail. pass criteria: 95th <= 320ms and cost delta <= 20% vs forecast or better.
[07:42] Omar Ruiz: that seems reasonable.
[07:48] Alex Chen: cool. quick queue on compliance: sophie, can you validate if sample audit logs + SOC2 pack cover your audit team? if there's an extra ask we'll tackle it.
[07:58] Sophie Kim: yes i'll check and get back by Monday.
[08:03] Dana Lewis: final question — if we decide to sign a 3 month reserved at the end of October, what's the minimum commit?
[08:12] Alex Chen: we typically offer a short-term reserved with a minimum baseline of one GPU pool unit equivalent. we can structure a bridged monthly contract to align with your billing cycle. i'll put specifics in the pricing doc.
[08:25] Raj Patel: ok, last thing — are there any gotchas we should know about during rollout?
[08:31] Priya Nair: watch for KV cache warm-up and kernel selection changes when switching quantization or model variants; we'll instrument additional tracing for your SRE team during the trial.
[08:44] Marta Ivanova: good. let's make sure trace hooks are active so we can tie latency blips to model changes.
[08:50] Elena Ortiz: agreed; we'll enable request-level trace ids and integrate with your tracing backend if you want.
[09:00] Alex Chen: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners in the chat.
[09:05] Marcus Holt: thanks all, we'll follow up with a meeting summary and the attachments.

End of transcript
